1599516403081834497 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 10
writing canonical resources is hard and confusing

thread of me thinking out loud about repeating, remixing, and the differences between:
- twitter threads (dated, can't edit)
- blog posts (dated, can edit)
- pages/canon (not dated, can edit)

===

1599516418898546688 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
anyway, I'm going to try rewriting this, mostly, not trying to edit the other one to fit a new container, partially because I'm way better at writing than editing (and I enjoy it more) and partially because then I'll have more potential for new fresh ideas
↓
1599516420198387712 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 
although actually... maybe that's just not true. I've had lots of fresh ideas in the course of editing old posts

and sometimes those ideas are so fresh they then make it hard to publish the thing because what felt almost-done now feels woefully inadequate
↓
1599516421649682432 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
which is an argument in favor of just publishing things now

eg I started trying to edit this thread into a blog post and ended up flipping inside out and rethinking the whole frame.
https://t.co/MxMdZp6s8J
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: coercion = "the exploitation of the scarcity of another, to force the other to behave in a way that you want"  (working draft, edited from some chats)  (this is in the context of other-coercion; self-coercion needs a slightly different definition) 🧵 https://t.co/TCc1WEnwzR]
↓
1599516423717810176 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
but part of what makes things difficult I think IS actually the aim of creating a CANONICAL resource

that was easy to write as a thread, since it was overtly a draft, but with my blog posts I feel they want to be more DONE before I publish them
https://t.co/EUvFYcEAa7
  [Quoting @m_ashcroft: I’m noticing a desire in myself to write comprehensive, ‘canonical’ essays on Alexander Technique, which each time I notice I choose not to do.  I’m happy to repeat myself and rewrite things over and over as I get better at communicating this stuff, perfectionism be damned.]
↓
1599516425982738432 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 6 🔁 1
part of the magic of being unable to edit twitter threads is that they HAVE to always only be a snapshot of how you were seeing it at the time. they can't be "kept up to date with the latest insights"
↓
1599516427316494336 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 
but weirdly it feels more easy to publish a page on the complice site that I could edit later, than a blog post that I could edit later.

I think that's partially because many of my reads come from the post being sent as a newsletter....
↓
1599516428771610624 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 
...but also... a blog post FEELS like a final thing, but because it DOES have a date on it, it becomes complex to edit it because I neither want to imply that: 1. I stand behind all confusions remaining post-edits
2. I already had shit figured out years ago
↓
1599516430625828864 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
somehow there's a sweet spot where something can be written as a snapshot of my learning at a point in time, and also its potency and clarity stands the test of time and it becomes "canon"

I feel like I really achieved this here:
https://t.co/MyrnAMacBb
↓
1599516432127373312 [2022-12-04] @Malcolm_Ocean 
that post now contains one [EDIT] parenthetical, but otherwise remains essentially the same except for maybe a few links added to pieces I hadn't yet written

years later I reflected about the nature of unintegrated understandings:

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand traces a 15-year evolution from abstract aspirations about 'collective consciousness' (2010) to concrete experiences of emergent group cognition on Twitter. The boundary object is Tasshin's 2022 tweet defining internet participation as 'learning to notice, harmonize with, and participate constructively in a self-organizing, emergent collective consciousness.' The arc is constructive rather than dialectical—people aren't arguing about whether collective consciousness exists, but rather reporting lived experiences of it, developing vocabulary for it, and building infrastructure to support it. The strand shows high evolution from vague buzzwords to specific phenomenology ('thoughts circulating between people,' 'one big giant brain') and practical applications (perpetual conversation rooms, coordination tools like ryzome).
